item.title: The Disturbance Was a Lawsuit
item.summary: On 11 August the CFTC invoked Section 8a(9) of the Commodity Exchange Act — an emergency power used four times between 1976 and 1980 and then not at all for 46 years — to order Kalshi to keep operating, declaring the New York Attorney General's enforcement action a "major market disturbance." Two days later a King County judge ordered Kalshi to shut off sports, elections and politics contracts in Washington by 2 September or face $120,000 a day. Both orders are in force. Underneath sits an unresolved split: the Third Circuit says sports event contracts are swaps subject to exclusive federal jurisdiction, the Southern District of Ohio says they are not, and three more circuits are holding the answer. Meanwhile the CFTC is rewriting the very rule its preemption argument depends on.
